key_insight: The paper proposes a new way to supervise reasoning models using rubrics instead of brittle full-chain rationales, making self-distillation more reliable and less annotation-heavy. By conditioning learning on structured evaluative criteria, it aims to preserve useful reasoning while reducing noise from imperfect explanations.
problem_solved: It addresses the high cost and unreliability of chain-of-thought supervision in post-training, where annotations can be incomplete, noisy, or even incorrect. It also tackles the weakness of compressing reward signals into sparse or overly simplified feedback during reinforcement learning.
method: Use rubric-conditioned supervision to guide the model with structured criteria rather than relying solely on full natural-language rationales.
Apply self-distillation so the model can learn from its own outputs under rubric guidance, reducing dependence on expensive human-written chain-of-thought data.
Leverage evaluative feedback in a more informative form than a single scalar reward, helping the model learn what makes an answer correct or high-quality.
impact: For practitioners, this could lower annotation costs while improving the quality and robustness of reasoning-model post-training. It offers a practical middle ground between noisy rationale distillation and sparse reward-only training.
